chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, his uncle, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him). I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The footwear of the man happens to be torn, so he enters his hand and wipes the back of his foot, would that suffice him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

key_terms.أُجْزِئُهُ: Would it suffice/be sufficient for him

ai.seo_question: Is wiping the foot valid if the shoe is torn?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the criterion for valid wiping over torn footwear (khuff) is defined by the physical accessibility of the foot rather than the integrity of the shoe itself. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the requirement is to wipe the skin of the foot, and as long as the tear permits the hand to reach and wipe the dorsal surface, the ritual act is considered complete and sufficient for wudu.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far in Suleyman, from his uncle who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The footwear of the man happens to be torn, so he enters his hand and wipes the back of his foot, would that suffice him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ali ibn ’Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ja‘far ibn Sulayman, his uncle who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, if the back of one’s slipper is torn and he pushes his hand through the torn portion to wipe the back of his feet, is this acceptable?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is sufficient.’”
